newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-COURT RULING WILL KEEP 1998 SUPER BOWL IN SAN DIEGO.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-COURT RULING WILL KEEP 1998 SUPER BOWL IN SAN DIEGO.

text.p: The 1998 Super Bowl will be played in San Diego as planned after a Superior Court judge dismissed a lawsuit challenging a $78 million expansion project for Jack Murphy Stadium.
The National Football League had announced a contingency plan to hold Super Bowl XXXII at the Rose Bowl in Pasadena if the stadium construction was halted by the suit.
The San Diego Chargers had also said they would likely have to play elsewhere next season, probably in Los Angeles, if improvements to their home stadium was stopped.
Opponents had argued it was illegal for the city to start construction in December, before completion of a petition drive which would put the project to a public vote.

But Judge Anthony Joseph ruled it did not matter because a 1995 agreement between the city and the Chargers to expand the stadium was already in force before the projected cost of the project balooned from earlier estimates of $60 million.
The NFL obviously was pleased by the ruling.

"With construction going forward on schedule, the uncertainty regarding the condition of the stadium has been removed and we can proceed with plans to play Super Bowl XXXII in Jack Murphy Stadium," NFL Commissioner Paul Tagliabue said in a statement issued by the league.
"We look forward to a great Super Bowl week next January in the San Diego area."
